title: Curry Barker's Anything But Ghosts Sets 2027 Release
excerpt: Curry Barker's new horror comedy follows aspiring ghost hunters whose search for fame turns frightening. Its US theatrical release is set for May 7, 2027.
content:
Curry Barker announces Anything But Ghosts: horror comedy arrives in cinemas in May 2027

Director Curry Barker is preparing a new feature film following the success of Obsession: the horror comedy Anything But Ghosts, whose US theatrical release has been announced for May 7, 2027. Focus Features confirmed the date, while Boxoffice Pro reported that the film will also be screened in Barco's premium HDR format. The story follows a group of ghost hunters seeking fame, but their pursuit leads them into terrifying circumstances they cannot control. The cast includes Barker, Cooper Tomlinson, Violet McGraw, Chris Reinacher, Bryce Dallas Howard and Aaron Paul. On November 16, TheWrap reported that Matthew Lillard had also joined the cast.
Focus Features announced that it holds the worldwide rights to the film, while international distribution will be handled by Universal Pictures International. The May 7 date refers to the nationwide US theatrical release, and separate dates for individual international markets have not been specified in the official announcement. The release schedule outside the United States will depend on announcements from the international distributor and local cinema operators. The project has been presented as a title intended for theatrical distribution, with an international rollout planned through Universal's distribution network.

Fake paranormal investigators face real threats

According to the official Focus Features synopsis, a group of ghost hunters desperate for fame finds itself in a situation where events quickly spiral out of control. In an interview with GQ, Barker summed up the premise as a story about fraudsters posing as ghost hunters who then encounter real ghosts. TheWrap reported that Barker and Tomlinson play two fake paranormal investigators who accept a job involving dangerous phenomena in a couple's home. Their initial deception thus becomes the source of a genuine threat, and the protagonists must navigate circumstances for which they are unprepared. The official description does not reveal details about the characters, the setting or the development of the supernatural events.

A horror comedy bearing Barker's creative signature

The project has been described in film announcements as a horror comedy, and Barker's previous work provides context for this combination of genres. In his GQ profile, the director highlighted his attraction to simple premises that can be presented clearly but then create room for unexpected consequences. The idea of fraudsters falsely investigating the paranormal before encountering genuine supernatural phenomena fits that approach. A comparison with Obsession reveals a shift in themes: the previous film explored a desire that takes on dark consequences, while the new project starts with deception and an attempt to achieve fame. Barker told GQ that he wants to continue creating original stories, even after his success opened the door to larger productions.

Cast and creative team

Focus Features lists Barker and Tomlinson among the cast members, alongside Violet McGraw, Chris Reinacher, Bryce Dallas Howard and Aaron Paul. Barker is responsible for directing and writing the screenplay, while Tomlinson is his screenwriting collaborator, and both also appear in front of the camera. On November 16, TheWrap reported that Matthew Lillard had joined the project, although details about his character have not been released. Lillard is known to audiences for playing William Afton in the film adaptations of Five Nights at Freddy's, and he also appeared in the new adaptation of the novel Carrie for Prime Video. His involvement expands the previously announced cast list, but it is not yet known how his character will fit into the central plot.
The production is credited to Roy Lee, Steven Schneider, Jason Blum, Adam Hendricks and Greg Gilreath. Focus Features states that the project brings together the production companies Spooky Pictures, Blumhouse and Divide/Conquer, alongside Image Nation and Barker's production label That's a Bad Idea. Daniel Bekerman, Curry Barker, Cooper Tomlinson and Ben Ross are listed as executive producers. The screenplay was developed by Barker and Tomlinson, making the continuation of their collaboration one of the project's key elements.

Premium HDR release and Barco technology

On November 24, Boxoffice Pro reported that Barco had confirmed the film's inclusion in its premium HDR exhibition programme. The same system was also used for Barker's previous title, Obsession, according to the specialist publication. Barco's approach is based on its patented Lightsteering technology, which distributes light across different parts of the image to highlight bright elements while preserving detail in darker areas. According to information reported by Boxoffice Pro, peak brightness can be more than six times greater than with traditional projection, while retaining detail in the shadows. HDR, or High Dynamic Range, expands the contrast between the brightest and darkest parts of an image and can increase the amount of visible detail within a frame.
Barco presents the technology as a way of preserving both very bright and very dark parts of a scene simultaneously on the big screen. This is a projection format, not a different version of the story or a special edited cut. Actual availability of this type of screening will depend on cinemas equipped with the appropriate technology and participating in the distribution. The specific visual appearance of the cinematography and the way Barker uses light will only become apparent when the film reaches audiences.

From online sketches to studio productions

According to a profile published by GQ, before achieving wider success in filmmaking, Barker worked with Tomlinson on the comedy channel That's a Bad Idea. The channel reached nearly two million subscribers, and the duo published hundreds of sketches, including content about attempts to break into the film industry. This work allowed them to communicate directly with audiences and quickly test comedic ideas. GQ notes that Barker developed a preference for dialogue that does not explain every detail, instead leaving audiences room for their own interpretations through the online format. The same profile states that he began making films as a teenager before moving to Los Angeles, where he studied acting and worked on auditions before turning his attention to directing.
GQ reported that the budget for the new film was £3.8 million, the largest amount Barker had worked with up to that point, and that filming was completed in Vancouver towards the end of the summer. His career path included independent projects and working with limited resources, while his later success enabled him to collaborate with larger production partners. The director also discussed his working methods with GQ: he edits his own films and is drawn to long takes and scenes filmed in a single continuous shot. These techniques are part of his creative signature, although it has not yet been revealed to what extent they will influence the finished look of the new film.

The success of the previous film and expectations for the new title

Obsession brought Barker wider international recognition. Focus Features described the previous film as a worldwide success that marked his collaboration with the studio, while GQ reported that it became the most successful title in the distributor's history. Following that result, Barker chose not to make a sequel but instead to develop a separate story with different characters and a different genre emphasis. In an interview with GQ, he said that he wants to continue making original films rather than immediately turning to established franchises. The new project therefore continues his collaboration with the same creative partner while exploring a different premise.
